changeChecks.reason: The 337 to 341 window for p075's s0080 campaign is source-backed: Haedong (Xiankang 3/337, citing Jinshu), Tongjian (Xiankang 5/339), Samguk (Gogugwon 9/339 on the 331 count, verified against the year-12 Longcheng move in 342), and the forward Jinshu antecedent (Yu Liang's death in 340, recognition in 341). No other supported reading falls outside it. The event note, however, calls Haedong a primary witness and counts Samguk as independent support, so it is amended.

The 338 to 342 homage window for p075's s0081 is supported: 338 from Haedong's next year, 340 from Samguk's explicit year 10, and 341 or 342 from the forward Jinshu reading. The event note only repeats the campaign rationale, mislabels Haedong as a primary witness and does not state Samguk's dependence on Tongjian, so a corrected homage-specific note is supplied.

The owner p075 as commander, the target Goguryeo and the other party p111 are correct for s0080. The 337 to 341 interval honestly covers the competing readings, but the shared event note has the same witness-characterization error as claim-429 and is amended identically.

p075 as host receiving homage from p112 matches s0081, and the 338 to 342 interval is supported. The note's mislabeling of Haedong, its unstated Samguk dependence on Tongjian and its omission of the homage readings need the same homage-specific amendment as claim-430.

p111 King Zhao begging a covenant in s0080 is correctly owned, and the 337 to 341 window is supported by the cited witnesses. Only the event note's witness characterization needs correcting, as in claim-429.
p111 sending his heir in s0081 is correctly owned, with the dependent 338 to 342 window. The event note needs the homage-specific correction given for claim-430.
p112 the heir attending Huang's court in s0081 is correctly owned, and the 338 to 342 window is supported. The event note needs the homage-specific correction given for claim-430.

Adding AD 337-341 and AD 338-342 while keeping AD 339 and AD 340-341 matches the supported campaign and homage windows and preserves p075's unchanged dated events in s0073 to s0088. No amendment to these values is needed.
p111 takes part in both the s0080 campaign (337 to 341) and the s0081 homage (338 to 342), so both hints are source-backed and do not choose a single year.
p112 appears only in the s0081 homage, so AD 338-342 alone is the correct hint; the campaign window is rightly not added to the heir.

references.reason: I re-read the full linked chapter. Year 9 records the invasion to Xincheng and the covenant plea, and year 10 records the heir's homage. The year-12 entries (the Longcheng move and the sack of Hwando, which Tongjian dates to 342) confirm the 331 accession count, so years 9 and 10 are 339 and 340. The year-9 and year-12 wording closely follows Tongjian, so this is not independent of it.

I re-read the full linked chapter. Under the Xiankang heading, year 3 (glossed Gogugwon year 7, with a note that Tongjian has year 5) gives the campaign and next-year homage, citing the Jinshu. Its year-2 gloss (Gogugwon year 6) implies the same 331 accession count. It is a later compilation, so it is a competing reading, not a primary witness.

I re-read the full linked chapter. The campaign appears in the Xiankang 5 (339) winter entry with Liu Xiang's mission, Yu Liang's death opens Xiankang 6 (340), Liu Xiang reaches Jiankang and Huang is recognized in Xiankang 7 (341), and the Yeweng Pass raid is in Xiankang 6, winter month 10. These dates support the 339 reading and the 340 to 341 forward-antecedent endpoints.

findings.problem: The event note begins 'Primary-witness uncertainty' and lists Haedong Yoksa among the witnesses, though it is a much later compilation that the packet's own haedong6 note calls not an independent contemporary witness. It also presents Tongjian and Samguk together as support for 339 without saying that Samguk's wording follows Tongjian.
findings.action: Replace only the event note with the amended campaign text. Keep the 337 to 341 interval, source date, owner, certainty and evidence unchanged.

findings.problem: The homage claims reuse the campaign note, which has the same witness-characterization error. It also never states the homage readings themselves, including Haedong's implied 338 lower endpoint and Samguk's explicit year-10 (340) entry, so the 338 endpoint is not justified in the record.
findings.action: Replace only the event note with the amended homage-specific text. Keep the 338 to 342 interval and all other fields unchanged.

before.unresolvedReason: Jinshu109 s0080 says 其年 after the Yu Liang death/royal-recognition narrative (340or later by narrative order), while ZZTJ96 explicitly places this Goguryeo campaign and King Zhao’s peace plea under Xiankang5/339. The antecedent or conflicting chronology requires independent source resolution; neither witness is silently preferred.

after.event: Competing source readings are retained and no single year is selected. Haedong Yoksa, a much later Joseon compilation and not a primary witness, cites the Jinshu and files this campaign under Xiankang 3 (337), noting that Tongjian has year 5. Zizhi Tongjian places it in Xiankang 5 (339). Samguk Sagi records it in King Gogugwon's year 9 (339 on its 331 accession count), but its wording closely follows Tongjian, so it is not counted as an independent confirmation. Read forward from the Jinshu's own narrative order, after Yu Liang's death (340) and the court's recognition of Huang as King of Yan (341 in Tongjian), the campaign would fall in 340 or 341. This inclusive window spans those readings.

amendments.reason: Keeps the host's proposed source date, interval endpoints, owner, certainty and evidence unchanged. It replaces only the event note, which wrongly called Haedong Yoksa a primary witness and implied that Tongjian and Samguk are two independent confirmations of 339. Samguk's text follows Tongjian closely, and the packet's own reference note says Haedong is not an independent contemporary witness. The campaign note now states each reading and its basis.

after.event: Competing source readings are retained and no single year is selected. The heir's homage is dated only 'the next year' after the disputed campaign year. A forward reading of the Jinshu narrative order (campaign in 340 or 341) gives 341 or 342. This inclusive window spans those readings.
